image_description: A close-up view of an industrial sawmill operation. The foreground features a wooden conveyor track carrying rectangular planks of light-colored lumber. In the mid-ground, there are large, rusty circular saw blades mounted on heavy machinery frames. The background shows blurred industrial equipment and piles of wood debris/sawdust. The scene is dominated by earthy tones of brown, yellow, and rust.

artifact_observations.location: Mid-ground machinery supports and wheel axles
artifact_observations.reasoning: The mechanical connections between the large saw blades and their mounting frames appear physically implausible. Axles seem to float or merge into the frame without clear bearing structures. The geometry of the machine legs in the lower center is ambiguous and seems to melt into the ground/debris.
The wood grain on the planks is overly uniform and lacks the natural variation expected in cut timber. The edges of the planks are slightly soft and bleed into the conveyor structure.

artifact_observations.location: Junction of conveyor belt and support frame (lower left)
artifact_observations.reasoning: The boundary between the wooden slats of the conveyor and the metal/wood support structure below is indistinct, suggesting a fusion of materials rather than distinct mechanical assembly.

To verify the 3D spatial relationship between the overlapping saw blades and the conveyor, checking for depth bleeding or impossible overlaps.
To audit the connectivity of the machine parts, specifically checking if the wheels/blades are properly attached to the frames or if they exhibit floating/fusion artifacts.
To assess the realism of textures (wood, rust, metal) and identify any subtle generative noise or blurring inconsistencies.

Physical plausibility of conveyor belt structure
